claim: A repair this round created a new conflict at an edge. §4.11's epoch step (c) (l.7804-7806) says 'a building whose household count falls but not to zero takes a `relet` down … and `vacate` fires only when its last household leaves'. Neither has an exception, and §4.11's `LadderOp` `relet` (l.7860) bounds its `households` 'within §2.6's capacity', which §2.6 clamps to [1, capacity]. The VEL0-01 fix in §7.7's precedence (l.11379-11382) says a locked or pinned dwelling's last household leaves under a dossier fall by a `relet` down, and the building is 'never `vacate`d'. An epoch that follows §4.11 vacates a locked building and so changes a locked state, which §7.7 forbids. An epoch that follows §7.7 emits a `relet` to 0, which `LadderOp` does not admit.

claim: Two round-1 repairs disagree at the steepest site (VEW-03 × VEW-10). §4.2 S3 (9), *Every arc closed* (a mesa town, an island town filling its island): 'the stage walls nothing … its routes (5), picked by the land law on the whole contour as an unwalled town's are, enter across the barriers'. §4.3's new *class grade limit* makes 'an edge steeper than the routed class's grade limit … impassable to that route'. The steepest limit is `path`'s `rampMaxGrade` of 0.15 (V11 §3.24.5), on a lattice of about 25 m. So any lattice edge across a cliff, sheer or gorge face taller than about 3.75 m is impassable to every class, and F-ROUTE's last rung leaves the destination `unserved`. A mesa girt by such faces therefore gets no route in, against S3 (9)'s 'enter across the barriers'. EP-21 names 'a mesa town' as a B-EDGE fixture but gives no outcome that matches the generator. VPC-R1-02 (the wall grade of cliff-class arcs) is a different gap: its fix still leaves the sheer and gorge case, and any walled cliff-class mesa, to this rule.
required_change: §4.2 S3 (9), the *Every arc closed* sentence: replace 'enter across the barriers' with 'enter across the barriers where §4.3's class grade limit admits an edge — a marsh, a cleft or ramp in a cliff, an island town's landings ((13)) — and otherwise take F-ROUTE's last rung (`unserved`, reported; §5.2), so a mesa girt by faces steeper than `path`'s `rampMaxGrade` over one lattice step has no road in at generation and says so'. claim: The intermediate terraces of §4.7 *Levelling and retaining walls* have no record and no datum. The repair (VEW-05) widened the rule: 'A step above `stepMaxCm` takes ⌈step ÷ `stepMaxCm`⌉ − 1 intermediate terraces, each at least `minTerraceDepthM` deep and each edge a wall of at most `stepMaxCm`, laid inside the two units'. The same applies to a levelled unit's edge against unlevelled ground. A levelled unit holds one datum (`Plot.platformCm`, `Block.platformCm`, §2.5), and 'the one reader of levelled heights', `levelledGroundCm`, returns 'the datum of the levelled plot, block or ward holding p'. A terrace laid inside a unit therefore has no height of its own anywhere. On both sides of an intermediate wall `levelledGroundCm` reads the same unit datum, so `stepProfile(wall)` derives a step of 0 for a wall raised to hold up to `stepMaxCm`. A building, V04 knot or shadow on the terrace reads the wrong level. EP-24's fixture 'a step above 2 × `stepMaxCm`' has no stated heights to check.
required_change: §4.7 *Levelling*: state that an intermediate terrace splits the unit it is laid in along the contour into two levelling units, each with its own datum (as V07 §3.8a (2) splits a house platform: 'each levelled at its own datum, the footprints split with it by the base's stepped-wing rule'). For a plot, add a stepped datum to §2.5 — `Plot.platformSteps?: { line: ChainRef /* the intermediate wall */; datumCm: Cm }[]`, written by S11's levelling, in the plot's leaf digest; likewise `Block.platformSteps` for S10's — and have `levelledGroundCm` return the datum of the step region holding p. claim: The closed-arc rules repair r1 added (VEW-03) contradict the wall grading. §4.2 S3 (4) counts 'a cliff, a gorge, a marsh, a sheer face, a river's banks round a loop' as closing arcs and allows picks only on approachable arcs. S3 (9) says 'Every arc closed (a mesa town; …): the stage walls nothing — no Enceinte is recorded for it and it has no gate', and §4.4 S5a step 1 says 'a stage whose every arc closes walls nothing and records no enceinte'. But §4.4 S5a step 1 itself says 'a steep slope or marsh closes behind a light wall', §4.8 *Graded by stretch* lays 'a lighter parapet on cliff tops, steep slopes and waterfronts', and V11 §3.16.1's rows give `cliff` 'closes: yes, wall: parapet' and `steepSlope`/`marsh` 'closes: yes, wall: light'. Only `sheerCliff`, `deepWater` and `gorge` close with no wall. So a mesa ringed by `cliff`-class arcs (≥ 60 % over ≥ 6 m, below the sheer test), or a marsh-ringed town, is walled by §4.8 and V11 but unwalled with no Enceinte by S3 (9). If walled, it has no gate, because no pick may fall on a closing arc: an undefined outcome either way.
required_change: In §4.2 S3 (9) and §4.4 S5a step 1, make 'every arc closed' mean every arc whose defensibility row (V11 §3.16.1) has wall `none` (`sheerCliff`, `deepWater`, `gorge`); for those, keep the text ('walls nothing … no Enceinte … no gate'). Add, in (9): 'Where every arc closes but some carry a parapet or light wall (the `cliff`, `steepSlope` or `marsh` rows), the stage is walled on those arcs by §4.8's grade and records its Enceinte. It takes N₁ = 1 gate, picked on its walled closing arcs, least defensible first (`steepSlope`, then `marsh`, then `cliff`; then the pick contour's order), its route reaching it within §4.3's class grade limit, else by F-ROUTE's ladder. Reported (`W_WALLED_BY_BARRIERS`).' In (4), state which arcs are approachable: those whose row does not close, plus a sea or lake shore as (4) already counts it. Add a mesa below the sheer test and a marsh-ringed town to EP-21's fixtures.
